# 1 Maccabees Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_005_page_001.jpg

---

1. When the nations around them heard that the altar had been rebuilt and the sanctuary rededicated as before, they were furious.
2. They plotted to wipe out the descendants of Jacob living among them, and the killing began.
3. Judas struck the Idumeans at Akrabattene — they had been harassing Israel. He hit them hard, broke them, and stripped their dead.
4. He hadn't forgotten the sons of Baean either — they had been a constant trap for the people, ambushing them on the roads.
5. He penned them up in their towers, besieged them, put them under the ban, and burned the towers down with everyone inside.
6. He crossed into Ammonite territory, where Timothy was commanding a large, strong force.
7. They fought again and again. The Ammonites broke and ran every time. Judas crushed them.
8. He seized Jazer and the villages around it, then headed back toward Judea.
9. Meanwhile the Gentiles in Gilead were massing against the Israelites on their borders, trying to wipe them out. The Israelites fled to the fortified stronghold of Dathema.
10. They got a letter to Judas and his brothers: "The nations around us have closed in to destroy us.
11. They're coming to seize the stronghold we've taken shelter in. Timothy is their commander.
12. Come and rescue us. Many have already died.
13. All our people in the land of Tobias are dead — wives and children taken captive, possessions gone, about a thousand people killed."
14. They were still reading the letter when another group of messengers arrived from Galilee with torn garments, carrying the same kind of news:
15. "People from Ptolemais, Tyre, and Sidon have joined every Gentile in Galilee against us. They want us dead."
16. When Judas and the people heard all this, a great assembly gathered to figure out what could be done for these kinsmen in danger and under attack.
17. Judas said to his brother Simon: "Pick your men and go rescue our people in Galilee. Jonathan and I will go to Gilead."
18. He left Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah in command with the remaining forces to defend Judea.
19. His orders to them were clear: "Keep the people safe. Do not engage the Gentiles in battle until we're back."
20. Simon got three thousand men for the Galilee mission. Judas and Jonathan got eight thousand for Gilead.
21. Simon moved into Galilee and fought battle after battle against the Gentiles. They broke before him.
22. He drove them back to the very gates of Ptolemais. About three thousand Gentiles died; he took their plunder.
23. He gathered up all the Jews in Galilee and in Arbatta — wives, children, everything they owned — and brought them back to Judea with great joy.
24. Judas Maccabeus and his brother Jonathan crossed the Jordan and marched three days into the wilderness.
25. They ran into Nabateans who greeted them peacefully and gave them the full report on what had happened to their people in Gilead:
26. many were besieged in Bosora, Bosor in Alema, Caspho, Maked, and Carnaim — all big, well-fortified cities —
27. and others were shut up in the other cities of Gilead. The enemy plan was to attack the strongholds the next day, take them all, and kill every man in a single day.
28. Judas wheeled his army immediately and came at Bosora across the desert. He took the city, killed every man, stripped it bare, and burned it.
29. They marched out by night and kept going until they reached the stronghold.
30. Dawn came. They looked up. Ahead of them was a force that couldn't even be counted — carrying scaling ladders and siege machines to take the stronghold. The fighting was already underway.
31. Judas saw that the battle had started. The cries of the city were going up to heaven like trumpets and great noise.
32. He told his men: "Today you fight for your brothers."
33. He led three columns charging into the rear of the enemy force, sounding trumpets and shouting in prayer.
34. When Timothy's army recognized Maccabeus, they ran. He struck them hard. Eight thousand of them died that day.
35. He swung south to Maspha, attacked it, took it, killed all the men, looted it, and burned it.
36. He swept on — Caspho, Maked, Bosor, the rest of the cities of Gilead, one after another.
37. After that, Timothy reassembled another army and set up camp facing Raphon, across the ravine.
38. Judas sent scouts to look at the force. They came back: "Every nation around us has gathered under him. An enormous army.
39. They've brought Arab auxiliaries too. They're camped on the far side of the ravine waiting to come at you." Judas marched to meet them.
40. Timothy told his commanders: "If Judas crosses the ravine first, we can't handle him — he'll overwhelm us for certain.
41. But if he hangs back and camps over there, we cross to him and we win."
42. As Judas came up to the ravine, he put the officers on the bank and issued one order: "No one stops. Everyone crosses. Everyone fights."
43. He went first. All the men followed. The Gentiles shattered before them, threw down their weapons, and ran for the temple precinct in Carnaim.
44. They took the city and put the temple precinct to the torch with everyone in it. Carnaim was finished. It could not stand before Judas.
45. Judas assembled all the Israelites in Gilead — old and young, wives and children and everything they owned — a great convoy — and set out for the land of Judah.
46. The road brought them to Ephron — a large city, heavily fortified, sitting squarely across their path with no way around it, right or left. The only way was through.
47. The people of the city locked the gates and barricaded them with stones.
48. Judas sent a message offering terms: "Let us through. We're heading home. We won't hurt anyone. We'll just walk through." They refused to open.
49. Judas ordered the whole camp to halt and set up right there.
50. They camped and fought the city all day and all night. It fell.
51. He killed every man, razed the city to the ground, stripped it, and marched through on the road made over the bodies of the slain.
52. They crossed the Jordan into the broad plain facing Beth-shan.
53. All the way back Judas gathered the stragglers and kept encouraging the people until they reached Judea.
54. They went up to Mount Zion with joy and celebration and offered burnt offerings, because every last man had come home alive.
55. Now while Judas and Jonathan were away in Gilead and Simon was in Galilee before Ptolemais,
56. Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah heard the reports — the victories, the battles, the glory.
57. They said: "Let's make a name for ourselves too. We'll go fight the Gentiles around us."
58. They gave orders to their troops and headed for Jamnia.
59. Gorgias came out of the city to fight them.
60. Joseph and Azariah broke and ran. They were chased back to the borders of Judea. About two thousand Israelites died that day.
61. A terrible defeat — because they hadn't listened to Judas and his brothers and had charged out on their own.
62. They did not come from the family of men through whose hands Israel had been saved.
63. Judas and his brothers were honored throughout all Israel and among all the Gentiles — wherever people heard their name.
64. Men crowded around them and praised them.
65. Judas marched with his brothers against the Idumeans in the Negeb. He struck Hebron and its surrounding villages, tore down the strongholds, and burned the towers.
66. He struck camp and pushed into Philistine territory through Marissa.
67. That day some priests fell in battle — they had wanted to win glory and gone out to fight without any order to do so.
68. Judas turned toward Azotus in Philistine country. He tore down their altars, burned their idols, plundered the cities, and came back to Judea.
